subject: physics
title: Slit Dash
summary: Aim a laser so a bright stripe hits the target, find where two colours meet and set a meter for two waves.
ncertRef: Section 10.5, Interference of light waves and Young’s experiment
learningOutcome: The student can use x = nλD/d to find a wavelength or a fringe position, find where bright fringes of two colours coincide, and find the intensity from the path difference.

levels.title: Kestrel’s range
levels.adds: Baseline: the n-th bright fringe is at x = nλD/d, so the colour of the light decides where a stripe lands (Ex 10.4).
hints: Bright fringes are at x = nλD/d, so λ = xd/(nD).
Keep every length in the same unit before you divide; mm to m or nm to m.
A test shot tells you where the fringe lands for the colour you have chosen.

levels.title: The double lock
levels.adds: New idea: two colours have bright fringes at the same place when n₁λ₁ = n₂λ₂ with the smallest whole numbers (Ex 10.6).
hints: Both colours need a whole number of wavelengths: n₁λ₁ = n₂λ₂.
Reduce λ₁ : λ₂ to the smallest whole numbers to get n₂ : n₁.
Then x = n₁λ₁D/d for the nearest place to the centre.

levels.title: The power meter
levels.adds: New idea: for a path difference Δ the brightness is cos²(πΔ/λ) times the maximum K (Ex 10.5).
hints: The phase difference is φ = 2πΔ/λ, and I = 4I₀cos²(φ/2).
At Δ = λ the brightness is K = 4I₀, the maximum.
So I/K = cos²(πΔ/λ). Work in degrees: π × Δ/λ is 180° × Δ/λ.

levels.title: Lamps or lasers
levels.adds: New: two lamps are incoherent: their intensities just add to 2I₀ everywhere, while coherent beams give 4I₀cos²(φ/2) (Section 10.4).
hints: Coherent sources keep a fixed phase difference; independent bulbs do not.
Incoherent: the intensities add, I₀ + I₀ = 2I₀.

misconceptions: Bright fringes get wider the further they are from the centre
Two different colours always make the same fringes
Brightness at a path difference of λ/2 is half the maximum
